question.text: A Cat II AIF has appointed the same independent valuer for five consecutive financial years. Under SEBI's current framework governing valuer engagement for Cat I/II AIFs, what is the correct position?

answer.text: The AIF must rotate the valuer; IPEV best practice combined with SEBI emphasis on independent rotation discourages indefinite single-valuer engagements
There is no restriction; indefinite engagement is explicitly permitted
Rotation only applies to Cat III AIFs
The manager must appoint exactly three valuers every year on a round-robin basis

explanation.text: The Logic: Per PDF Section 11.12 and SEBI circulars, the emphasis on external INDEPENDENT valuations, disclosure of deviations, and the Sep 2024 amendment all reinforce a rotation principle. IPEV and IVCA best practices recommend periodic valuer rotation to prevent familiarity bias. While SEBI does not mandate a fixed rotation period for Cat I/II (unlike statutory auditor rotation), the principle of independence pushes fund managers toward rotation and toward using two valuers in parallel for cross-validation. The Trap: 'No restriction' ignores the independence principle; rotation applies across all AIF categories not just Cat III; three valuers round-robin is not a rule. The correct answer captures the regulatory direction of travel. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same rotation best-practice. Statutory auditor rotation under Companies Act 2013 Sec 139 (5-year individual / 10-year firm) is a common analogue tested in CA exams. Manager's Pro-Tip: Document your rotation policy in the fund's Valuation Policy Manual, approved by the Board of the Trustee. LPs increasingly ask about valuer-tenure limits during DD — have a 5-year tenure policy ready.
